t: This is the tomb of Granville Sharp, in the churchyard of All Saints. Sharp was an English scholar and philanthropist, and one of the first campaigners against the slave trade in Britain. His cause began in 1767, when he defended a badly injured enslaved man from Barbados in a legal case against his master. After that he kept looking for test cases that challenged the legal justifications for slavery. In 1769 he published the first tract in England that explicitly attacked slavery itself. He died in 1813, and he is buried here.
